Not all statements are created equal. Here are some criteria that we use to help establish a hierarchy of important statements to fact-check:

  • Amounts that can be checked and verified. Example: Cabinet Secretary Phyllis Kandie promises Ksh18bn for orphans, disabled kids
  • Statements that are causing the most buzz. Example: Who really controls Ward Development Funds?
  • Statements that have gone viral on social media or are being repeated often by public officials. Example: Will Kenya Olympic champs get Sh1bn bonus
  • Statements that can be proved or are well supported by facts — is the statement a prediction, or subjective? Example: Is Kenya increasing funding to the health sector?
  • Numbers that may have been manipulated to support a partisan message. Examples: Uhuru's maternity care numbers exaggerated; Has Kiambu collected Ksh4.7bn in revenue?

Members of the public can also suggest claims to be fact-checked, by:

  • Emailing the newsdesk at hello@pesacheck.org
  • Emailing the managing editor at doreen@pesacheck.org
  • Contacting us on PesaCheck's WhatsApp tipline at +254 780 542626

If claims from the public meet the public interest criteria, they'll be looked into, and feedback provided on the channel it was shared.
headline: Identifying Claims to Check
